column4: after a managed create, apply and sync both find nothing to do.
declining a managed scale leaves the file and Capella alone.
an entry with an id (deployed once, then deleted outside cbctl) is not replaced.
keys added by commands land where sync writes them, so a later sync finds the file in sync.
create of a name that is in the file but was never deployed replaces the entry, keeps its children and records the id.
a scale below the limit is refused before the file or Capella changes.
overlap with a cluster in another project only warns.
an overlapping range typed in the wizard is re-asked (only the CIDR), and the suggested default is used.
a range overlapping a cluster that is in Capella but not the file exits 3 and suggests a free range.

the wizard asks, plans, confirms, deploys and records the cluster. cbctl's wizard runs when NAME is missing and asks for it first; it has no "cluster type" or "support plan" question (--free-tier and --support-plan are flags).
provider defaults (gcp region, pd-ssd disk), the medium size, the support plan, and --size dev as a singleNode cluster.
a capella.yaml that is already invalid stops create before any question is asked.
conflicting flags exit 3 instead of re-asking, even on a terminal.
a CIDR with host bits set is re-asked, then the default range is accepted and the cluster deployed. (cbctl's wizard runs when NAME is omitted.)
each bad value exits 3 with its reason, and neither the file nor Capella changes.
a name in the file points at cluster update; a name only in Capella points at sync. Both exit 4 with no writes.
a P6 disk's fixed size is never sent on update, and --disk-size on it exits 3.
managed update shows the diff, records the new values and sends one PUT.
update with no flags on a terminal asks each value, Enter keeps it.
cluster update offers no flag for a value Capella cannot change.
zones and the schedule stay behind; the clone gets its own CIDR and no schedule is written.
after a clone, plan and apply see no change, sync is in step, and cloning again is refused (exit 4) with no writes.
--server-version latest sends no couchbaseServer.
the confirmation counts and names the buckets that go with the cluster; one DELETE, no separate bucket deletes.
the summary says the on/off (hibernation) schedule is deleted with the cluster, and the DELETE keeps snapshot backups.
the table, the total, the JSON services and an unknown cluster.
the plan line, "scale out", one PUT with both groups, and the file.
the added group is written in normal form (sorted services, given compute and disk); apply and sync then find nothing to do.
an existing group of another size, a node count over the limit and an unknown service exit 3 and change nothing.
a singleNode cluster has exactly one group.
more than 27 nodes in total exits 3; a free-tier cluster exits 4; neither writes.
one PUT with the other groups; the file loses the group.
removing a data group the buckets need is blocked.
a turned-off cluster cannot be scaled (exit 4, the file is unchanged).
every verb's help has an example; the scaling guide shows group add.
the PUT body is the observed cluster with the file overlaid: support is merged key by key and the observed service groups are kept.
a field the file leaves out keeps its observed value.
the PUT is the observed body with the file's changes overlaid, sent with If-Match.
a node-count change has no settings note and its progress says "scaling".
a description change says it starts a Capella job (text and JSON notes) and does not call the progress "scaling".
changing an immutable field is blocked (exit 4, or exit 3 when the file is already invalid offline) and nothing is written.
the update waits for a busy cluster before the PUT and for the job after it.
a new name without an id plans a create and hints at pinning the id.
a pinned id renames the cluster in place.
re-applying after a support change writes nothing.
5 → 4 nodes passes both guards, prints the checks, lists the cluster as destructive in the prompt and sends one PUT.
3 replicas need 4 data nodes, so a declarative 4 → 3 is blocked with exit 4 and nothing is written.
a bucket with 3 replicas blocks 4 → 3; -o json reports status blocked and nothing is written.
--step -1 runs the scale-in checks and then scales.
--step +1 at --max is a successful no-op.
--all-groups steps each group by one, in one PUT.
a cluster still scaling is waited for first, and the step is counted from the node count it reaches.
every -o json outcome of --step matches scale.schema.json.
more CPU and RAM per node is a "scale up" and nothing else.
a cpu/ram change is a "scale up"; the PUT keeps the node count and the disk.
a disk change is sent in the provider's shape.
a smaller disk is blocked (exit 4, no writes).
scale out one group and scale up another in one PUT.
32 → 16 GB per data node halves the data service, so the bucket memory must fit half of today's total.
re-applying after a compute change writes nothing.
12,288 MB of buckets fit in 4/5 of 20,480 MB, and the checks line gives both numbers and the replica requirement.
allocated == projected is allowed; one MB more is blocked.
no flag lets the last data group go.
